text: There is a sound in the Pacific that has repeated for decades, and no one knows what makes it.
In 1991, scientists started listening to the ocean with old Navy microphones.
And this sound was already there.
A long train of rising tones, each a few seconds long, again and again.
Loud enough to be recorded across the whole Pacific.
Scientists traced it to a remote spot in the far South Pacific, thousands of kilometers from any coast.
And it's seasonal. It peaks in spring and autumn.
Nobody knows if the source changes, or just the ocean that carries it.
The best guess: volcanic activity on the seafloor nearby.
But no one has proven it.
Since 1991, it has slowly been getting quieter.
The agency's own archive says it plainly. The origin is unresolved.
So what is still singing down there?
